analysis.title: The Flow Show: DEM fatale
key_insights: BofA stays risk-off until central bank rate hikes end (41 in the past 6 months), the 10-year UST yield falls below 4.5% and oil falls below $80/bbl, which would reverse the tightening of financial conditions.
If Nov CPI and payrolls are weak, BofA says the Dec Fed/ECB/BoJ hikes could be the last hikes, and risk assets could start a year-end rally around Thanksgiving.
BofA flags a 'double-top' in the S&P 500 Equal-Weighted Index (SPW) and notes no one is talking about a 'big top'.

NDX is down 15% over the past month and tech leaders broke: NVDA below $200, TSM below $400, MAGS below $70. BofA says SPX holds above 7,000 as long as recession odds stay low (banks IXG hold $125, mid-caps MDY $666, junk bonds JNK $92).

BofA reads the midterm Democratic wave as a shift from populist capitalism to populist socialism, with taxes and regulation set to rise (negative for EPS). It calls the 2026 midterms peak AI equity concentration.
BofA's midterm signals: gold over oil, lower yields, tech bonds over tech stocks, consumer stocks over energy, small caps over monopolies, long Europe and long China tech.
Hyperscaler capex consensus is $239bn in '24, $412bn in '25, $820bn in '26 and $1.3tn in '27. Free cash flow is -$63bn in '26 and -$252bn in '27.
AI debt issuance is rising: global debt issuance $297bn YTD vs $110bn in '25, US debt issuance $217bn YTD, equity issuance $100bn YTD, and annualized buybacks only $14bn YTD vs $90bn in '25.

BofA says bond and credit markets want AI capex and issuance to slow. Slower capex would favor MAGS 'spenders' over AI 'builders' such as semis and neoclouds. AI stocks return once yields reset lower and there is no recession.
Data centers are electorally unpopular (76% oppose a new data center in their community). BofA says the AI capex forecast for '28 of about $2tn is a little too high.
The Fed hiked on Sep 16 and a Dec 9 hike is 64% priced. ECB (76%) and BOE (50%) decide on Dec 17 and BOJ (68%) on Dec 18. There have been 55 hikes this year against 11 expected in January.

BofA says oil needs to fall sharply for the tightening cycle to end before a credit event or recession. It recommends selling energy and buying consumer, and 'sell oil, buy bonds' while waiting for lower oil and yields before adding risk.

BofA's 2027 scenarios are bubble, breadth and bust. It says consensus conviction in the bubble case (50% 'no landing' in the Oct FMS) has peaked, breadth optimism is still high (40% soft landing), and fear of a hard landing is too low (6%).
Downward revisions are expected to 2027 forecasts for 5% US nominal GDP and 45% global tech EPS growth, after 94% in 2026.

BofA's long-term call is to buy gold. The new Congress is sworn in Jan 3 and the US hits the $41.1tn debt ceiling around Feb 1. Gold rose 12% and 17% in the 3 months before the 2011 and 2023 debt ceiling standoffs.
Weekly flows: $140.4bn to cash (7th biggest weekly inflow on record), $89.2bn to stocks, $11.6bn to bonds, $0.1bn to gold, $1.8bn out of crypto.

Global equities took in a record $265.6bn over 4 weeks ($317.1bn to passive). US equities took in $92.3bn over 4 weeks, and China stocks a record $85.9bn over 4 weeks (attributed to 'national team' buying).
EM debt had a $6.1bn outflow, the 6th biggest on record and the first since Jul'26. Europe equities had a $1.3bn outflow. Tech had a $9.8bn inflow and $44.6bn over 4 weeks.

BofA Bull & Bear Indicator rose to 7.2 from 7.1 (Neutral signal). Equity flow is at the 95th percentile and FMS positioning at the 100th, while global stock index breadth is at the 21st percentile (bearish).

BofA Global Breadth Rule: net 16% of global equity indices are oversold. A buy signal needs net 88% oversold, which BofA says requires SPX below 7,323 and UK/European bourses down another 3-4%. SOX is 17% below its 200dma, and 20-25% below has been a good entry point since '96.

BofA private clients: $4.6tn AUM, 65.8% in stocks (3-month low), 17.7% in bonds (7-month high), 9.3% in cash (record low). They bought TIPS, bank loan and muni bond ETFs and sold EM debt, staples and utilities ETFs.
2028 election odds on Polymarket: Democrats win 68%, Republicans 31%. Ossoff leads the Democratic nomination at 28% and Vance the Republican nomination at 35%.
'Bro Billionaire' stocks (META, NVDA, PLTR, TSLA, HOOD, ARKK, COIN, APO, BX, ORCL, XBT) peaked in Oct'25 and are up 18% since inauguration, trailing the Trump 'Base' (small caps), which is up 21%.

YTD returns to Nov 4: oil 58.8%, global stocks 8.8%, US stocks 7.4%, US dollar 3.2%, cash 3.2%, HY bonds -0.1%, IG -1.4%, govt bonds -2.0%, gold -5.3%, bitcoin -13.0% (the ranked table shows bitcoin at -8.5% and gold at -6.2%).

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler capex rises to $820bn in '26 and $1.3tn in '27, and BofA's bubble scenario cites AI as the new railroads and a US government backstop of AI.
tension_points.bear_case: Free cash flow turns negative (-$63bn in '26, -$252bn in '27) and debt issuance is surging. Bond and credit markets want capex to slow, and data centers are electorally unpopular.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Yields reset lower with no recession, which would bring AI stocks back at a slower buildout pace.

tension_points.theme: Central bank hikes and year-end rally
tension_points.bull_case: If Nov CPI and payrolls are weak, the Dec Fed/ECB/BoJ hikes are the last hikes and risk assets start a year-end rally around Thanksgiving.
tension_points.bear_case: The Fed has hiked and a Dec 9 hike is 64% priced. 55 hikes have been seen this year against 11 expected, and oil is up 58.8% YTD.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The 10-year UST yield staying above 4.5% and oil above $80/bbl, which BofA says keep financial conditions tight.

tension_points.bull_case: Consensus forecasts a 40bps drop in UST yields and 15% SPX EPS growth in '27, and Goldilocks unlocks value in small and mid-caps.
tension_points.bear_case: Bonds and voters end booms and bubbles, and credit tightening means no AI boom. Downward revisions are coming to 2027 forecasts for 5% US nominal GDP and 45% global tech EPS.
tension_points.what_invalidates: SPX holding above 7k while recession odds stay low (IXG $125, MDY $666, JNK $92) keeps the no-retreat view intact. A break of those levels would invalidate it.
